plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the AlexNet convolutional neural network architecture using a 3D volume diagram viewed in perspective. A left-to-right flow begins with a sheared input photograph representing the 224×224×3 input image, followed by a sequence of three-dimensional feature map volumes rendered as parallelogram-faced blocks in light teal (#d3edeb) for the main face and darker teal (#a0d9d3) for the depth layers, while orange (#d18362) and dark orange (#773c23) parallelogram blocks represent convolutional filter kernels applied at each stage. The feature map volumes progressively shrink in spatial resolution while increasing in depth, with labeled dimensions 55×55×96, 27×27×256, and 13×13×384 corresponding to the first three convolutional stages of AlexNet. Ellipsis (…) markers appear within the teal volume stacks to indicate that only a representative subset of the channels is depicted. A “Conv 5×5” annotation above one inter-stage region identifies the kernel size of one convolution, and black arrows with arrowheads indicate the forward data flow between stages. This figure introduces the AlexNet architecture, showing how successive convolution and pooling operations reduce spatial resolution while extracting increasingly abstract feature representations.

interactions.teaches: The learner follows the left-to-right AlexNet pipeline and sees that early convolution and pooling stages trade shrinking spatial resolution for increasing channel depth.

interactions.label: Convolutional stage
interactions.teaches: Selecting a convolutional stage connects the kernel annotation to its output tensor, making clear which feature-map dimensions result after that stage.
Rotating the highlighted tensor exposes its depth axis, so the learner can compare channel growth against the shrinking spatial height and width.

demo_steps.title: Stage 1: first feature maps
demo_steps.narration: The 224×224×3 image is transformed by the first convolutional stage into a 55×55×96 feature tensor. The highlighted block shows a large drop in spatial size and a jump from 3 input channels to 96 learned channels.

demo_steps.title: Stage 2: deeper features
demo_steps.narration: After pooling and the Conv 5×5 stage, the selected tensor is 27×27×256. Spatial dimensions keep shrinking while the channel dimension grows substantially.

demo_steps.title: Stage 3: compact high-depth representation
demo_steps.narration: The next selected convolutional tensor is 13×13×384. The block is spatially compact but deep, illustrating how AlexNet builds many feature channels over a smaller image grid.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique CNN-architecture layout matching the source: left-to-right horizontal flow, blocks sitting along a shared lower baseline, labels in black serif text rotated about -30 degrees for dimension annotations and about -35 to -45 degrees for operation labels. Overall world span about x=0 to 15, y=0 to 5, z=0 to 1.5. Input image slab at x≈0.8, y≈2.6, size about 2.5 high × 2.5 wide, very thin depth 0.08, tilted in-plane so its left edge is vertical and its top edge slopes upward right; texture should be a dark warm candle-like image with orange/yellow glow and black lower region. Orange convolution blocks use front face #d18362, side/top depth faces #773c23 or #9a5434, black outlines. Approximate tensor display sizes should preserve the source proportions rather than literal numeric scale: stage 1 55×55×96 as a tall upright block at x≈3.6, y≈1.45, front width 0.45, height 1.15, depth 0.55; stage 2 27×27×256 at x≈5.3, y≈1.25, front width 0.75, height 0.65, depth 0.55; stage 3 13×13×384 at x≈7.1, y≈1.15, front width 0.95, height 0.35, depth 0.45; stage 4 13×13×384 at x≈8.9, y≈1.15, same as stage 3; stage 5 13×13×256 at x≈10.4, y≈1.15, front width 0.75, height 0.32, depth 0.40. Fully connected/classifier stacks are light teal front faces #d3edeb with darker teal sides #a0d9d3 and black outlines. First and second 4096 stacks at x≈11.9 and x≈12.8, each height about 3.2, width 0.22, depth 0.15, split into lower and upper slabs separated by an ellipsis/dotted gap; labels 4096 above each. Two 1000 stacks at x≈13.8 and x≈14.7, each height about 1.7, width 0.22, depth 0.15, also split with ellipsis; labels 1000 above. Black arrows connect each stage along the baseline. Dimension labels: input 224×224×3, then 55×55×96, 27×27×256, 13×13×384, 13×13×384, 13×13×256. Operation labels along bottom: Conv 11×11 Stride 4, MaxPool, Conv 5×5, MaxPool, Conv 3×3, MaxPool + FC, FC, FC, Softmax. For the layer slider overlay, stage 1 should show kernel 11×11, stride 4, output 55×55×96; stage 2 should show kernel 5×5, output 27×27×256; stage 3 should show kernel 3×3, output 13×13×384, while still honoring the requested visible Conv 5×5 overlay for the second selected stage.
interactionPlan.notes: Render blocks as custom BufferGeometry cuboids/parallelepipeds with black edge outlines to reproduce the textbook’s hand-drawn oblique 3D style. The data-flow animation should highlight one stage at a time with a bright outline or glow and a moving pulse along the connecting arrows; do not move the blocks themselves. The slider highlight should override or synchronize with the animation highlight when the learner selects a stage. The selected tensor drag should rotate only the highlighted tensor in place, with a reset when another tensor is selected, so the overall architecture layout remains recognizable. Add a small floating overlay card near the selected tensor containing kernel size and output dimensions; keep all original dimension labels visible.

discrepancies: The generated input candle image is a simplified stylized reconstruction and is smaller/less photo-like than the large realistic image slab in the source.
A yellow highlight box and explanatory overlay card are added around the active tensor; these are not present in the original figure and visually clutter the first stage.
The fully connected and softmax columns use separated cuboid segments with dotted ellipses instead of the source's continuous tall thin columns with jagged break marks.
The overall composition is more horizontally compressed and front-facing than the source, with weaker oblique depth and a less dominant input image.
Some operation labels and arrows are shifted from the source alignment, especially around the FC/Softmax region.
evaluation.notes: The AlexNet pipeline is clearly recognizable with correct major tensors, dimensions, and colors, but the input image, FC break styling, added highlight/overlay, and some proportions reduce fidelity.
action_items: Remove or make optional the yellow highlight frame and overlay card when matching the static source figure.
Make the input image slab larger and more photo-like, with proportions closer to the source.
Replace the dotted split FC columns with tall thin columns using jagged break marks as in the original.
Tune the camera and object spacing to better match the original oblique composition and relative scale.

feedback.rationale: The AlexNet concept and plan are correct, but the critic identifies concrete rendering fidelity issues and hallucinated overlays that the generator can fix.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the AlexNet convolutional neural network architecture using a 3D volume diagram viewed in perspective. A left-to-right flow begins with a sheared input photograph representing the 224×224×3 input image, followed by a sequence of three-dimensional feature map volumes rendered as parallelogram-faced blocks in light teal (#d3edeb) for the main face and darker teal (#a0d9d3) for the depth layers, while orange (#d18362) and dark orange (#773c23) parallelogram blocks represent convolutional filter kernels applied at each stage. The feature map volumes progressively shrink in spatial resolution while increasing in depth, with labeled dimensions 55×55×96, 27×27×256, and 13×13×384 corresponding to the first three convolutional stages of AlexNet. Ellipsis (…) markers appear within the teal volume stacks to indicate that only a representative subset of the channels is depicted. A “Conv 5×5” annotation above one inter-stage region identifies the kernel size of one convolution, and black arrows with arrowheads indicate the forward data flow between stages. This figure introduces the AlexNet architecture, showing how successive convolution and pooling operations reduce spatial resolution while extracting increasingly abstract feature representations.

- Drag to rotate a selected tensor block: inspect how the depth (channel) dimension grows relative to the shrinking spatial height and width across AlexNet's early layers

discrepancies: The input image panel is much smaller and flatter than the source, where it is the dominant tall slab with a visible dark side face.
The fully connected teal stacks use separated rectangular slabs with ellipsis dots but lack the distinctive zigzag break marks shown in the source.
The generated figure adds a yellow tensor highlight and explanatory overlay card that are not present in the original and visually clutter the central labels.
Several lower operation labels are split or shifted compared with the source sequence, making the MaxPool/Conv label grouping less faithful.
The first few convolutional blocks and arrows are more horizontally aligned and compressed than the more strongly stepped oblique layout in the source.
evaluation.notes: The AlexNet pipeline is clearly recognizable with correct major tensors, dimensions, and interactions, but the input slab scale, FC break marks, and added instructional overlays reduce visual fidelity.
action_items: Increase the input image slab height and visible depth so it dominates the left side like the source figure.
Add the zigzag break marks to the teal FC and Softmax stacks instead of relying only on ellipsis dots.
Make the yellow highlight and explanatory overlay optional or hidden by default to better match the original static figure.
Adjust the lower operation labels so combined labels such as MaxPool/Conv 5×5 and MaxPool/Conv 3×3 align more like the source.
